title: attack
summary: Benilla defines the melee wire: SMSG_ATTACKSTART (two full guids), SMSG_ATTACKSTOP (two packed guids + dead u32), SMSG_ATTACKERSTATEUPDATE (hitInfo, packed guids, sub-damage fold), SMSG_AI_REACTION, and CMSG_ATTACKSWING/ATTACKSTOP. MSUI's CombatPackets.cs parses start/stop/swing byte-identically (including the sub-damage absorb/resist summing and trailing zero+spellId+blocked words) and WorldSession sends swing/stop; swing-error opcodes are also mapped to messages.

openItems.text: SMSG_AI_REACTION: opcode-table entry only (Net/Opcodes.cs:290), no handler in the Program.Net.cs dispatch - the creature aggro/alert notice (raw u64 guid + u32 reaction) is never parsed
